01.actor: A groom and bride who came before Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
01.event: A groom reported finding no blood on his wedding night and the bride said she was still a virgin.
01.turn: Rabbi saw their faces were blackened by famine, so he had them bathed, fed and watered before sending them back to the room.
01.outcome: The groom then found blood, and Rabbi told him to go take possession of his acquisition, citing Lamentations 4:8.
01.summary: During a drought, a groom told Rabbi he found no blood on his wedding night, and his bride insisted she was still a virgin. Rabbi saw that their faces were dark from hunger and had them bathed, fed and given drink, then sent back to the room. This time the groom found blood, and Rabbi told him to go and enjoy his acquisition, quoting a verse about skin shriveled like wood.

02.event: Rabbi once ruled in accordance with Rabbi Elazar on a woman's menstrual status.
02.turn: He then remembered that Rabbi Elazar's colleagues disagreed with him.
02.outcome: He said Rabbi Elazar is worthy to be relied upon in exigent circumstances.
02.summary: Once Rabbi ruled that the law follows Rabbi Elazar. Afterward he remembered that Rabbi Elazar's colleagues disagreed with him. He nonetheless said that Rabbi Elazar is worthy to rely on in times of need.
02.missing: The details of the case in which he ruled are not given.

03.event: A woman who had seized a silver cup as partial payment of her marriage contract also demanded sustenance and came before Rava.
03.turn: Rava ruled that part of the money does not count as all the money, so her seizure did not bar her claim.
03.outcome: Rava told the orphans to go and give her sustenance.
03.summary: A woman seized a silver cup toward her marriage contract and also demanded sustenance from her late husband's heirs. She came before Rava, who told the orphans to go and give her sustenance, since no one worries about Rabbi Shimon's view that partial money is not like all the money.

04.actor: A man who came before Rabban Gamliel
04.event: A man told Rabban Gamliel he had found an unobstructed orifice, and Gamliel answered with a parable about a man walking in the dark who finds a door open if he diverts it.
04.turn: Gamliel suggested the man had diverted his approach, so the open finding proved nothing.
04.outcome: No outcome for the man is stated; a second version only changes Gamliel's wording.
04.summary: A man came to Rabban Gamliel claiming he had found an open orifice on his wedding night. Gamliel asked whether he had diverted his approach and told a parable of a man in the dark who finds a door open only if he diverts it. A second version has Gamliel say it was done intentionally. We are not told what became of the man.
04.missing: What happened to the man and his claim afterward.

05.actor: A woman who visited her husband's grave
05.event: The text alludes to an incident in which a woman removed her husband from his grave.
05.turn: Only a gesture at the incident appears in the Hebrew; the translation adds that she had intercourse with a guard and then suggested disinterring her husband to cover for a missing body.
05.outcome: Used to show that even in mourning one may sin.
05.summary: The Rabbis' view is illustrated by an incident of a woman who removed her husband from his grave. According to the translation's explanation, she met a man guarding a body of an executed person, they had intercourse, and when that body was taken she proposed digging up her husband so the guard could claim he had done his job. It is told only in allusion.
05.missing: The Hebrew only alludes to the incident; the details come from the translator's gloss.

06.event: He asked Rabbi Eliezer whose request for water to honor first when both parents ask, and then took the same question to Rabbi Yehoshua.
06.turn: He pressed Rabbi Yehoshua about a divorced mother.
06.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua sarcastically told him he was obviously a widow's son and to pour water for them and squawk at them like chickens.
06.summary: A widow's son asked Rabbi Eliezer which parent to serve first if both ask for water. Eliezer said to set aside his mother's honor for his father's. He asked Rabbi Yehoshua, who said the same, and when the man asked what if his mother was divorced, Yehoshua remarked that his tear-filled eyelashes showed he was a widow's son and sarcastically told him to serve both.

07.actor: Rav Yosef and his student Abaye
07.event: Rav Yosef said he had never heard a certain teaching, and Abaye reminded him that he himself had taught it.
07.turn: Abaye recalled the context in which Rav Yosef had stated it, including the brothers case and Rav Yehuda's explanation.
07.outcome: No outcome is stated; the remembered teaching is simply laid out.
07.summary: Rav Yosef claimed he had not heard a certain teaching. His student Abaye reminded him that he had said it to them, and recalled the brothers-at-father's-table case and the explanation Rav Yosef gave. The passage ends with the reminder, not Rav Yosef's reaction.
07.missing: Rav Yosef's reaction to being reminded.

08.event: Rava first thought famine was not like war regarding a wife's testimony of her husband's death, but a woman came before him and said her husband died in a famine.
08.turn: Rava questioned her and she admitted he could not have survived the little flour she left, showing she had not seen him die.
08.outcome: Rava retracted and said famine is like war.
08.summary: Rava thought a wife's report of death in a famine should be trusted, unlike in war. Then a woman told him her husband had died in a famine. He asked whether she had done well to flee and leave him with a little flour, and she answered that he could not have survived that. Rava saw she had only inferred the death and changed his ruling to treat famine like war.

09.missing: The passage is a legal argument with a passing example of Rabbi Tavla seeing a bolt and saying nothing, used as a proof and then rejected.

10.event: As he went up to Eretz Yisrael, he said he had been spared one curse, then, when ordained, two, and when seated on the calendar council, three.
10.turn: Each milestone avoided a part of the prophecy of Ezekiel that threatened those who would not be in the council, register or land of Israel.
10.outcome: He was spared all three curses.
10.summary: When Rabbi Elazar ascended to Eretz Yisrael he said he was spared one curse. When he was ordained he said he was spared two, and when he was seated on the calendar council he said three. The three correspond to the verse in Ezekiel that threatens false prophets with exclusion from the council, the register and the land.

11.actor: A father and mother marrying off their minor daughter
11.event: The father wanted her to marry his relative and the mother wanted her to marry hers, and the father yielded under pressure.
11.turn: During the festive meal for the mother's relative, the father's relative came up to the roof and betrothed her.
11.outcome: The Gemara assumes the father did not desire this betrothal, given his word and the effort spent on the meal.
11.summary: A couple disagreed about whom to marry their young daughter to, and the wife forced her husband to accept her relative. While they ate and drank at the betrothal feast, the husband's relative came to the roof and betrothed the girl. The Gemara reasons that the father did not want that betrothal, since he had given his word and prepared the meal.

12.event: Mar Yehuda visited Rav Huna bar Yehuda's house and saw people carrying among trees that were not planted in rows.
12.turn: He asked whether Rav Huna did not follow Avimi's view.
12.outcome: Rav Huna replied that he followed Rav Naḥman, who permits it.
12.summary: Mar Yehuda came to Rav Huna bar Yehuda's house and saw people carrying among trees that were not planted in rows. He asked whether Rav Huna did not accept Avimi's ruling. Rav Huna answered that he followed Rav Naḥman's view, which permits it.

13.event: Rav Kahana held beer belonging to an orphan and delayed selling it until the Festival.
13.turn: He reasoned that although it might sour a little, it would fetch cash then.
13.outcome: No result is told; only his reasoning is given.
13.summary: Rav Kahana was holding beer that belonged to an orphan, Rav Mesharshiyya bar Ḥilkai. He held off selling it until the Festival, saying that although it might sour, it would bring in cash. We are not told how it turned out.

14.missing: This is Rav Yosef's reply in a legal dispute citing a past ruling by Rav Yehuda, not a narrative in itself.

15.actor: Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda and Rabba
15.event: A bill of divorce dated by the governor of Bascar was sent by Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda to Rabba for a ruling.
15.turn: Rabba answered that even Rabbi Meir concedes since the governor is of that kingdom.
15.summary: A bill of divorce had been dated by the name of the governor of Bascar. Rav Naḥman bar Rav Ḥisda sent the question to Rabba. Rabba replied that even Rabbi Meir would accept it, since the governor belongs to that kingdom.
15.missing: The people involved and what happened to the couple are not given; it is a case with a ruling.

16.event: A man told those present that his property should go to Toviya, then died.
16.outcome: Rabbi Yoḥanan said Toviya has come, with no worry that another Toviya was meant.
16.summary: A man said at his deathbed that his property was for Toviya, and he died. Toviya came to claim it. Rabbi Yoḥanan said that Toviya has come, so there is no need to worry that someone else was meant.

17.event: Rabbi Zakkai taught a baraita before Rabbi Yoḥanan that the area between side posts and beneath a crossbeam is a karmelit.
17.outcome: He told him to go out and teach it outside the study hall.
17.summary: Rabbi Zakkai recited a baraita before Rabbi Yoḥanan, holding that the space between side posts and under a crossbeam is a karmelit. Rabbi Yoḥanan rejected it and told him to go teach it outside.

18.missing: The passage only asks how the Israelites knew the Jabesh-gilead girls were virgins and gives a method; it narrates no event.

19.actor: A man who sold his property intending to move to Eretz Yisrael
19.event: He sold his property with the intention of ascending but ultimately did not go.
19.turn: The question arose whether he could undo the sale.
19.outcome: Rav Ashi ruled that if he had wanted to, he could have gone, so the sale stands.
19.summary: A man sold his property planning to go up to Eretz Yisrael but in the end never went. Rav Ashi said that if he had wanted he could have ascended, so the sale stands. A second version words this as a question, leaving room to cancel if something outside his control prevented him on the way.

20.actor: Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, and Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter
20.event: Rabbi Elazar saw Nakdimon's daughter gathering barley from between horses' hooves in Akko.
20.turn: Her fall from great wealth to this poverty struck him.
20.outcome: He recited a verse about her, reading 'kids' as 'bodies'.
20.summary: Rabbi Elazar swore that he saw Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter picking barley out from between the hooves of horses in Akko. She had once been enormously wealthy. He applied the verse about following the flock to her, reading it as having to feed her own body from animals' leftovers.
